module_title: Northern Plains & Peninsular Plateau - Basic Understanding
introduction: India's physical landscape is largely defined by two massive contrasting regions: the highly fertile, flat Northern Plains formed by river deposits, and the ancient, stable, table-like Peninsular Plateau in the south.

core_concepts.title: The Northern Plains
core_concepts.description: Formed by the interplay of three major river systems: the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra. They brought down massive amounts of alluvium (fertile soil) from the Himalayas, creating one of the most densely populated and agriculturally productive regions in the world.

core_concepts.title: The Peninsular Plateau
core_concepts.description: A tableland composed of old crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks. It was formed due to the breaking and drifting of the ancient 'Gondwana land', making it the oldest landmass in India.

core_concepts.title: Two Divisions of the Plateau
core_concepts.description: The Narmada river roughly divides the plateau into two parts: The 'Central Highlands' to the north (sloping towards the Ganga plain) and the 'Deccan Plateau' to the south (a triangular landmass).

core_concepts.title: Western vs. Eastern Ghats
core_concepts.description: The Deccan Plateau is bordered by the Western Ghats on the west and the Eastern Ghats on the east. The Western Ghats are higher and continuous, while the Eastern Ghats are lower and broken (discontinuous) by rivers flowing into the Bay of Bengal.

important_entities.name: Majuli
important_entities.significance: Located in the Brahmaputra River in Assam, it is the largest inhabited riverine island in the world, formed by the changing channels of the river in the plains.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because Meghalaya is in the Northeast, students assume it is part of the Himalayas. It is NOT. The Meghalaya (or Shillong) Plateau is actually an eastward extension of the Peninsular Plateau.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The Western Ghats have a higher average elevation (900-1600m) compared to the Eastern Ghats (600m).

exam_strategy_tips: A frequent MCQ asks for the oldest landmass of India: Always choose the Peninsular Plateau (not the Himalayas).
Remember that the Deccan Trap region is famous for 'Black Soil' which is ideal for growing cotton.
